text:
The Star Tribune ran an opinion piece on Saturday asking Quinn Hughes, still without an extension in Minnesota, to make up his mind. Hughes answered the only way a player can on a game night: a goal and an assist in a 6-2 win in Boston. The Wild went 3-0 on the road trip, have won eight straight away from home and are 15-3-4, with points in 11 straight, per NHL.com's Heather Rule.

The score was a lot kinder to Minnesota than the game was. Boston had 61 shot attempts to 46, owned the second period (1.53 expected goals to 0.48, the quality of chances), and won this game in 66% of our replays of every shot. The Wild kept scoring on shots that rarely go in. Ryan Hartman opened it in the first. Hughes scored 53 seconds into the second on a 2% chance, and Blake Coleman's slap shot, a 3% chance, made it 3-0 67 seconds later. Fraser Minten got one back on the power play, but Hartman scored again at 10:00 of the second, and after David Pastrnak made it 4-2 early in the third, Danila Yurov scored twice to put it away.

The two goalies were the gap. Jeremy Swayman allowed five goals on 24 shots, about 2.4 more than those shots deserved. Jesper Wallstedt, on his birthday, stopped 30 of 32 for his 14th win of the season and robbed Marat Khusnutdinov on a 51% look in the second, the best chance of the night. Ten Wild players had a point, with Kirill Kaprizov adding two assists to his scoring run, and Brock Faber was back from injured reserve.

Boston has more to worry about than one night. Pastrnak has called the team's play "unacceptable" this week, and this was the second time the Wild have beaten them by a combined 10-3 this season. Minnesota goes home Tuesday to face a Nashville team that hasn't lost in seven.
headline: The Wild finish a perfect trip as Boston can't finish anything
